Write tx_fs_stub.c (begin/commit/abort log and return 0)
notes: Written. Compiles standalone; needs kernel headers to build into the module.

title: Study overlayfs internals: lowerdir/upperdir/workdir + whiteouts
notes: Pure reading. Whiteout semantics decide P2-05's design.

title: Mount an overlay from kernel space per transaction
notes: VERIFIED in guest. Kernel creates <tx_root>/tx-<id>/{upper,work,merged}; the supervisor mounts the overlay in a private mount ns. do_add_mount() is NOT exported to modules, so a module cannot graft a mount however much of fs_context it may call - same split container runtimes use.

title: Abort: recursive discard of the upper layer
notes: VERIFIED: tests/p2/t02_abort.sh, 8 assertions. THE M1 DEMO. Creation, modification AND deletion all rolled back; tree byte-identical to before; upper/ drained.

title: Commit: merge upper into lower incl. whiteout handling
notes: VERIFIED: tests/p2/t03_commit.sh, 7 assertions. Whiteouts merge as unlinks. BUG FOUND+FIXED: overlayfs marks every NEW dir opaque, so treating opaque as wholesale-replacement broke an ordinary mkdir -p inside a tx.

title: Write-set tracking at inode granularity
notes: VERIFIED: the write set IS the upper layer - overlayfs already records one entry per modified object, so there is no write-path accounting to drift. tx_fs_writeset_count() walks it.

title: Read-set tracking
notes: PROMOTED from stretch: multi-agent is no longer optional - subagents make wait-for cycles reachable (docs/deadlock.md).

title: External-modification detection (i_version / mtime)
notes: VERIFIED: detect and report, do not refuse. Coarse mtime comparison; precise per-inode i_version needs the read set (P2-07). Policy belongs to P2-12 (OCC), not here.

title: Crash consistency: fsync ordering around merge
notes: Test by killing QEMU mid-merge. Good paper material.

title: Stackable passthrough FS prototype (wrapfs-style)
notes: STRETCH. Start from Zadok's wrapfs. Fallback: stay on overlayfs - system still complete.

title: Microbenchmark: CoW overhead + storage amplification
notes: VERIFIED: CoW is nearly free at the median (+34ns) and 3.6x worse at p99 (9155 vs 2562ns) -- the tail IS the copy-up. Storage amplification 4096x for a 1-byte edit of a 4096B file. An earlier version said 16x because it measured AFTER commit, which drains the upper layer.

title: Commit-time write-set intersection (OCC validation)
notes: PROPOSED (docs/deadlock.md section 2.2). OCC makes the DATA path deadlock-free by construction; the cost is starvation, not deadlock.
